title: Sridevi's birth chart
metaDescription: Sridevi's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.8° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 19.8° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 19.8° Leo — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 14.8° Virgo, Venus at 15.2° Leo, Mars at 10.5° Libra. Mercury in an earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Venus in a fire sign reads as attraction declared rather than implied; Mars in an air sign reads as effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Saturn — an opposition holding at 0.0°. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Saturn at 0.3°, and the Sun trine Jupiter at 0.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Saturn while both square Neptune. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Sun in Leo at 19.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Virgo at 14.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Libra at 10.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aquarius at 19.8° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 fire, 3 earth, 2 air, 1 water by element and 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.1° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
